summary.intent: Execute Phase 36 (inline-upload-progress) using the GSD workflow, then run a simplify/code-review pass and resolve all open PR review comments.
summary.outcome: Phase 36 completed with 2 plans executed across 2 waves, a React hooks order bug caught and fixed during verification, a full simplification refactor pushed, and all 7 PR review thread comments resolved.

repo: Upload store uses Zustand v5 — the two-arg equality form on bound hooks requires a ref-based workaround; `useStoreWithEqualityFn` from `zustand/traditional` is the official API but wasn't adopted here
cancelFile previously left entries in a 'cancelled' status; after simplify it removes entries atomically, eliminating the 'cancelled' status from the type union entirely
useFileUpload hook and uploadFiles() in upload.service.ts were dead code with zero consumers — removed in simplify pass
retryFile store action was unused after UploadListItem was fixed to use removeFile instead — removed
GSD phase worktrees are created at .claude/worktrees/agent-{id} and must be merged back to the feature branch after each wave completes

code.finding: Three useCallback hooks were defined after an early return — React Rules of Hooks violation caught by verifier; hooks moved before the early return
Extracted createUploadId() helper (was duplicated 3x) and isActiveUpload() predicate (was duplicated 5x); updateFileProgress now has a same-value guard to skip set() when progress unchanged
Zustand selector was returning a new array every render; fixed with ref-based equality check to prevent re-render on every progress tick
Race-condition cancel guard checked status === 'cancelled' but cancelFile now deletes the entry — guard updated to check !files.get(uploadId) instead
Retry created duplicate entries because retryFile reset the old entry while onRetry/handleFileDrop created a new one; fixed by using removeFile to delete the old entry before the new upload starts
Reduced-motion media query had specificity issues — fixed per CodeRabbit review comment
Progress bar aria-valuenow should be indeterminate (null) during encrypting phase, not 0 — fixed per CodeRabbit review comment

workflow: GSD verifier catches React hooks violations that TypeScript does not — verification step earned its place here
Simple one-file bugs found during verification can be fixed inline rather than going through gap-closure cycle
Worktrees from previous sessions should be pruned before starting new execution — stale worktrees accumulate
In parallel wave execution, agents commit with --no-verify; orchestrator runs pre-commit hooks once after each wave completes
classifyHandoffIfNeeded error is a Claude Code runtime bug fired after tool calls complete — treat as success if SUMMARY.md exists and commits are present

friction: Merging agent worktrees back to the feature branch caused STATE.md merge conflicts that had to be resolved manually
Zustand v5 bound hook equality-function typing is broken — required a ref-based workaround instead of the clean two-arg selector form
The cancelFile atomicity change had a subtle downstream breakage in the race-condition guards in useDropUpload that wasn't caught until a grep pass
Pre-commit hooks ran fine but the post-wave hook validation step still requires a stash/unstash dance to avoid dirty working tree errors
The stale cipher-box-wt-phase36 worktree from a previous session was present at wave start and needed manual removal
open_items: ci-debug worktree created at /Users/michael/Code/cipher-box-ci-debug on branch ci-debug — likely still exists and should be cleaned up once CI issues are resolved
useFileUpload.ts was deleted but the hook may have been part of the public API surface — confirm no external consumers before considering this fully closed
STATE.md markdown formatting was fixed in response to a review comment but the root cause (GSD tooling generating malformed markdown) was not investigated
File object retention in the upload store (needed for retry) was flagged by efficiency review but intentionally deferred — could be revisited if memory usage becomes an issue
